method: Action-level lexical and source-scoped comparison with canonical main corpus; this ledger records candidate distinctness, not editorial acceptance.

records.comparator_distinct_action_justification: Regional handmade ribbon/card crosses worn on St Patrick's Day; PATR-001 describes a local village patronal feast and related collective observance, not the badge-making action.
records.claims_limit: Irish historical practice; not currently universal

records.comparator_distinct_action_justification: Christmas-night candle at a window or table in Irish folklore differs from a Polish opłatek sharing, an Advent wreath prayer and Candlemas blessed candles.
records.claims_limit: Irish archival traditions; spirits/beliefs are recorded folklore, not Catholic doctrine

records.comparator_distinct_action_justification: Wigilia hay beneath the tablecloth is a separate symbolic action from sharing the opłatek wafer; it is also distinct from placing good-deed straw in an Advent manger.
records.claims_limit: Optional Polish household practice, without divination

records.comparator_distinct_action_justification: Branches of fruit trees put into water around St Barbara's day to flower near Christmas differ from the symbolic Advent manger of good deeds and Assumption blessing of herbs.
records.claims_limit: Vienna source; biography uncertain; not predictive magic

records.comparator_distinct_action_justification: Provençal cross-scored Christmas Eve bread including poor person's portion differs from French Epiphany galette and from general contextual regional feast foods.
records.claims_limit: Pre-midnight Christmas Eve Gros Souper, not Eucharistic or universally blessed bread

records.comparator_distinct_action_justification: Children setting out shoes for Three Kings gifts differs from Epiphany home-visiting singers and Epiphany cake; gift-receiving resemblance to St Nicholas is not the same feast or cultural custom.
records.claims_limit: Household cultural tradition, no automatic civic parade or miraculous delivery
